messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED · Sev=P1 · east-coast canary rollout failing — elevated 5xx and latency, pager: aj
aj: got the pager, joining now
aj: quick summary — flipped east-canary at 08:05, target 15% traffic. Error rate spiked around 08:08 to ~50% 5xx and latencies doubled.
maria: I have oncall overlap, jumping in
sam: seeing 502/500 from edge in us-east-1; traces show backend model process throwing decode errors / OOM-ish logs 
aj: rolling back canary flag now: /flags/canary-east -> false
aj: hitting internal toggle: curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"canary-east","value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
ops-sre: note — DNS weights still showing partial traffic to canary endpoints; TTLs are 300s so some PoPs still resolve to canary IPs
irene: is this CDN or DNS? Cloudfront edge caches may have sticky routes. I see old host header in edge logs.
aj: kill-switched the flag but clients still hit canary via cached DNS/edge routes — flag kill alone won't clear cached A records
maria: ok plan: 1) CDN invalidation, 2) emergency weight shift at routing layer, 3) reduce DNS TTL to 30s, 4) contact DNS provider to expedite
maria: doing CDN invalidation now: aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id D123 --paths "/*"
sam: lowering DNS TTL on east.example.redwood-ai to 30s via provider API
ops-sre: applied emergency weight shift: moved 100% traffic to blue-serving pool (confirmed)
incident-bot: PAGE: SEV1 · 08:12 UTC · ack by aj
customer-support: multiple customers reporting 504/502s (approx 12 orgs), some errors touching payments path — prepping outreach
maria: @customer-support please start outreach template A: "We're aware of intermittent errors in US-East, mitigation underway. We'll update within 30m."
aj: metrics: error rate down from 50% -> ~12% after weight shift + CDN invalidation; still tail errors at certain PoPs
sam: PR#1245 contains the model runtime change that landed in canary — preparing a rollback patch to remove the change from canary image
ops-sre: rolling back model runtime change in canary infra to prevent re-entrance once caches expire
aj: handing off to maria at 08:20 — I'll stay on standby for followups
maria: taking lead. Current: errors ~3.9%, CDN invalidation 60% complete, DNS TTL change propagated to authoritative provider, edge propagation ongoing
irene: follow-ups: add atomic cutover to runbook (so we don't rely on TTL churn), and add post-deploy checks for edge cache poisoning / host header mismatches
maria: holding all deploys to east region for 2h; will not re-enable canary until postmortem and verification
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED · SEV=P1 · mitigations applied: flag kill, CDN invalidation, routing weight shift, DNS TTL lowered. Monitoring in recovery. Owner: maria
aj: will add timeline and link to traces/logs in doc
maria: assigning postmortem to ops-sre; please publish in #postmortems within 48h and include customer impact list + root cause hypothesis
customer-support: will update affected customers that service has been restored and we're investigating cause
sam: adding follow-up action: add test that simulates TTL/dns caching during canary flips (tickets: INF-312)
maria: thanks all — great fast coordination. :thumbsup:
